title: Census Demographics: Florida & National County Analysis
text:
NoteMilestone #5 Dataset Scale: Analyzing 5,100+ FL Tracts & 3,100+ US Counties



This study leverages massive demographic datasets from the U.S. Census Bureau’s 2018–2022 American Community Survey (ACS) 5-Year Estimates across two geographic tiers: - Florida Census Tracts: High-density neighborhood resolution across 5,160 tracts in all 67 Florida counties. - United States National Counties: Nationwide comparative scale analyzing 3,222 counties across all 50 states, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico.

title: Census Demographics: Florida & National County Analysis
text:
Comparative Demographic Insights

State vs. National Dynamics: Across the 3,144 U.S. counties, the West and South exhibit the highest concentrations of Hispanic residents, but their underlying relationships with income differ substantially. In the West, Hispanic populations are distributed broadly across both agricultural communities and affluent coastal counties. In the South, Florida functions as an exceptional demographic anchor where high Hispanic shares span the entire economic spectrum—from agricultural hubs in Hendry and Hardee counties to major metropolitan centers in Miami-Dade, Broward, and Orange counties.
Neighborhood-Scale Nuance in Florida: While county aggregates provide an essential high-level overview, analyzing 5,160 individual Florida tracts reveals tremendous internal heterogeneity. Many tracts in Miami-Dade and Osceola exceed 80% Hispanic concentration while spanning household incomes from under $25,000 to over $150,000. The non-linear cyan loess trend illustrates that Hispanic representation in Florida is not confined to low-income census tracts, reflecting the robust, multi-generational economic diversity of the state’s Hispanic populace.
Regional Continental Divergence: In the Midwest and Northeast, the vast majority of counties report Hispanic shares below 10%, with elevated percentages tightly focused in specific urbanized manufacturing or transportation hubs. By contrast, Southern and Western counties exhibit substantial geographic clustering shaped by historic borders, migration channels, and expanding regional economic centers.

title: About This Project
text:
This project examines county-level demographic patterns across Florida using data from the U.S. Census Bureau’s 2018–2022 American Community Survey (ACS) 5-Year Estimates.

Data & Methodology

Source: U.S. Census Bureau 5-Year American Community Survey via tidycensus
Variables:

Total Population (B01003_001)
Hispanic or Latino Population (B03002_012)
Median Household Income (B19013_001)

Spatial Geometry: Florida county boundary shapefiles via tigris and Census TIGER/Line
Tools: R, tidyverse, sf, ggplot2, and Quarto
